### QUESTION 4 :

*Estimate the same demand model (using 2SLS with homogeneous passengers and a nested logit) as in the paper. To do this, you need to construct some of the explanatory variables, particularly the number of departures from each city. You can include fixed effects for cities and airlines. I provide an R code that performs the necessary calculations once all the variables have been computed (you may need to adapt it for your own specification).*

*Try all combinations of three instruments. Report the following in a table: • Mean own-price elasticity • Estimates of the price coefficient • The mean Lerner index • The J-test statistic Select the subset of instruments that provides the "most coherent estimates" based on the guidelines you explain in the text. In particular, estimate the median own-price elasticity across products and compare your results with those found in our paper.*

For this question, we will estimate the demand model using 2SLS with homogenous passengers and a nested logit. Before doing this we have to create new explanatory variables :

First, we reuse the code provided on Moodle to create several explanatory variables:

```{r}



mydatainit <- as.data.frame(bdd_airlines)[, -1]


###### Build ID
mydatainit$ID=seq(1,nrow(mydatainit))
nobs=max(mydatainit$ID)
mydatainit$MkID=as.numeric(factor(mydatainit$Market))
lis_markets=sort(unique(mydatainit$Market))
nbmkt=max(mydatainit$MkID)
mydatainit$FirmID=as.numeric(factor(mydatainit$Firm))
mydata=mydatainit[order(mydatainit$MkID,mydatainit$FirmID),]


### I recompute the shares
newtot=data.table(mydata %>% group_by(MkID) %>% summarize(totpax = sum(Pax)))
mydata <- merge(mydata,newtot,by="MkID")
mydata$lnsjs0=log(mydata$Pax/(mydata$MarketSize-mydata$totpax))
mydata$lnsjg=log(mydata$Pax/mydata$totpax)
mydata$OutsideShare=(mydata$MarketSize-mydata$totpax)/mydata$MarketSize
mydata$OwnShare=mydata$Pax/mydata$MarketSize




#### Nb products per market per firm and index of the first one ########
mydata$combination=paste(mydata$MkID,mydata$FirmID,sep="-")
mydata$one<-1
matproduct=data.table(mydata %>% group_by(combination) %>% summarize(nprod = sum(one), firmshare=sum(OwnShare), market = max(MkID), 
                                                                     firm = max(FirmID)))
matindp=matproduct[order(as.numeric(matproduct$market), as.numeric(matproduct$firm)),]

#startm[i] index of the first product proposed by a given firm in a given market
startm=rep(0,nrow(matindp))
startm[1] <-1
for(i in 2:nrow(matindp)){
  startm[i] <- startm[i-1] + matindp$nprod[i-1]
}
mydata <- merge(mydata,matindp,by="combination")
mydata=mydata[order(mydata$MkID,mydata$FirmID),]



missing_vars <- setdiff(names(bdd_airlines)[-1], names(mydata))

if (length(missing_vars) == 0) {
  message("OK: all original variables from bdd_airlines are present in mydata.")
} else {
  warning(
    "Some original variables from bdd_airlines are missing in mydata: ",
    paste(missing_vars, collapse = ", ")
  )
}


```

We will have to add other explanatory variables to estimate the nested logit demand :

#### Number of departures from each city

According to the empirical paper, we will also add the maximum number of of direct flights offered at the itinerary's endpoints by the same carrier offering itinerary j, called here `OriginConn` .

```{r}



dep_city_firm <- mydata %>%
  dplyr::filter(Stops == 0) %>%
  dplyr::select(MkID, Firm, Origin, Dest) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(Origin, Dest),
    names_to = "endpoint",
    values_to = "City"
  ) %>%
  group_by(Firm, City) %>%
  summarise(
    departures_nonstop = n_distinct(MkID),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

mydata <- mydata %>%
  left_join(dep_city_firm, by = c("Firm" = "Firm", "Origin" = "City")) %>%
  rename(dep_nonstop_origin = departures_nonstop) %>%
  left_join(dep_city_firm, by = c("Firm" = "Firm", "Dest" = "City")) %>%
  rename(dep_nonstop_dest = departures_nonstop) %>%
  mutate(
    dep_nonstop_origin = if_else(is.na(dep_nonstop_origin), 0L, dep_nonstop_origin),
    dep_nonstop_dest   = if_else(is.na(dep_nonstop_dest), 0L, dep_nonstop_dest),
    OriginConn = pmax(dep_nonstop_origin, dep_nonstop_dest)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(-dep_nonstop_origin, -dep_nonstop_dest)



```

#### Distance and square distance variables

According to the working paper, we include the variable Distance and Distance\^2 as observed as demand shifters. In the following code we compute the distance by computing the product between two variables `DirectDistance` and `ExtraMiles`. Indeed, we have assumed that `ExtraMiles` represents the multiplier of the direct distance for flight with stops and then standardize the variable to reduce the collinearity. This allows us to estimate more accurately the total distance traveled by the passengers, which is generally in case of stops higher distance than direct distance due to detours with stops.

```{r}


mydata <- mydata %>%
  mutate(
    Distance1  = DirectDistance * ExtraMiles,
    Distance  = as.numeric(scale(Distance1, center = TRUE, scale = TRUE)),
    Distance2 = Distance^2
  )

```

#### Dummy for companies

```{r}

# Classification acccording the paper
LEGACY_CODES <- c("AA", "DL", "UA", "US")  #The 4 main legacy
SOUTHWEST <- "WN"  #Hybrid system 
LCC_CODES <- c("F9", "NK", "B6", "SY", "VX", "G4", "U5", "FL")  # Low-cost
OTHER_CODES <- c("AS")  # Alaska et autres

mydata <- mydata %>%
  mutate(
    # Catégories exclusives
    is_Legacy = as.integer(Firm %in% LEGACY_CODES),
    is_WN = as.integer(Firm == "WN"),
    is_LCC = as.integer(Firm %in% LCC_CODES),
    is_Other = as.integer(Firm %in% OTHER_CODES),
    
    # Dummies individuels pour les carrier FE (comme dans le papier)
    # AA est la référence, donc pas de dummy AA
    DL = as.integer(Firm == "DL"),
    UA = as.integer(Firm == "UA"),
    US = as.integer(Firm == "US"),
    WN = as.integer(Firm == "WN"),
    LCC = as.integer(Firm %in% LCC_CODES),  # 1 dummy pour tous les LCC
    others = as.integer(Firm %in% OTHER_CODES)  # 1 dummy pour les autres
  )



```

#### City list

We will also create other variables to include fixed effects. In the working paper, they have added carrier and city as fixed effects. We already have the variable carrier in the data but not the city, therefore we include it in the data with the following code.

```{r}

list_city <- unique(c(mydata$Origin, mydata$Dest))[-1]
nbfe <- length(list_city)

cf <- matrix(0, nrow(mydata), nbfe)

for (j in 1:nbfe) {
  nom <- list_city[j]
  cf[, j] <- 1 * ((mydata$Origin == nom) + (mydata$Dest == nom))
}

cf <- data.frame(cf, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
colnames(cf) <- list_city

mydata <- cbind(mydata, cf)


```

#### Instruments

Now we will create the variables to get the instrument in the data. Firstly, in the data we already have the fuel cost per seat and in the following code we will create the dummy for monopoly, number of competing products, and the number of competitors of the same type (LCC and FSC).

By definition, a monopoly is defined when it exists only one company in a market. Therefore, we have constructed the dummy for monopoly by looking at the total number of firms for each market (defined as a non-directional pair of two cities).

The number of competing products is defined as the total number of products offered in a given market by rival airlines, excluding products offered by the same firm.

##### Dummy for monopoly and Number of competing products

```{r}

mydata <- mydata[, !duplicated(names(mydata))]


mydata <- mydata %>%
  group_by(MkID) %>%
  mutate(
    number_firm = n_distinct(Firm),
    Monopoly = as.integer(number_firm == 1),
    number_product = n(),
    CompetingProducts = number_product - 1
  ) %>%
  ungroup()


```

##### Number of competitors of the same type (LCC vs. FSC)

We construct the number of same type competitors by counting, within each market, how many airlines belong to the same carrier type (LCC vs FSC) and subtracting one to exclude the firm itself.

Here we include in the FSC group the 4 main legacy carriers and the Others, and we define the LCC group by the carriers defined as LCC, and we decided to exclude the Southwest Airlines (WN), as in the working paper they characterized WN as not being par of the 4 main legacy carriers, due to its hybrid system and is not part of the Others and LCC groups. Therefore, we have decided to create three categories to be in line with the paper : LCC, FSC and WN.

Additionally, we assume that :

B6 = Jet Blue NK = Spirit Airlines F9 = Frontier Airlines VX = Virgin Airlines SY = Sun Country Airlines G4 = Allegiant Air U5 = USA3000 Airlines AS = Alaska Airlines FL = Air Tran Airways UA = United Airlines DL = Delta Airlines AA = American Airlines US = US Airways WN = Southwest Airlines

```{r}

mydata <- mydata %>%
  # Definition of FSC
  mutate(
    FSC = as.integer(is_Legacy == 1 | is_Other == 1)
  ) %>%
  group_by(MkID) %>%
  mutate(
    n_FSC_m = n_distinct(Firm[FSC == 1]),
    n_LCC_m = n_distinct(Firm[is_LCC == 1])
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    SameTypeCompetitors = case_when(
      FSC == 1      ~ pmax(n_FSC_m - 1, 0),
      is_LCC == 1   ~ pmax(n_LCC_m - 1, 0),
      is_WN == 1    ~ 0,     
      TRUE          ~ NA_real_
    )
  )

```

#### 2SLS Regression :

##### Model 1 : Fuel_Cost_per_seat + Monopoly + SameTypeCompetitors

```{r}

list_regressors=paste("Price + lnsjg + Stops + OriginConn + Distance + Distance2 + DL + UA + US + WN + LCC + others",
                      paste(list_city, collapse = " + "),sep=" + ")

list_instruments1=paste("Stops + OriginConn + Distance + Distance2 + DL + UA + US + WN + LCC + others",
                        paste(list_city, collapse = " + "),
                        "Fuel_Cost_per_seat + Monopoly + SameTypeCompetitors",sep=" + ")

##### 2SLS ######
lhs <- "lnsjs0"
formula1 <- as.formula(paste(paste(lhs, list_regressors, sep = " ~ "), list_instruments1, sep = " | "))
nliv1 <- ivreg(formula1, data = mydata)

#summary(nliv)
summary(nliv1, vcov = sandwich, diagnostics = TRUE)
stderr_d1=sqrt(diag(nliv1$cov.unscaled))
lambda1=1-nliv1$coefficients[3]
alpha1=-nliv1$coefficients[2]
theta0d1=nliv1$coefficients

##### Some outcomes ########

#### Markups
mydata$markup1=-lambda1/alpha1/((1-lambda1)*mydata$firmshare/(1-mydata$OutsideShare)+lambda1*mydata$firmshare-1)
mydata$mc1= mydata$Price - mydata$markup1
mydata$lerner1=(mydata$markup1)/mydata$Price
summary(mydata$lerner1)
summary(mydata$mc1)

#### Price elasticities
own_price_elas1=(alpha1*mydata$Price)*(((1-lambda1)/(1-mydata$OutsideShare)+lambda1)*(mydata$OwnShare)-1)/lambda1
mydata$own_price1=own_price_elas1

summary(mydata$mc1)
summary(mydata$lerner1)
mean_own_price_elas1 <- mean(own_price_elas1)
summary(own_price_elas1)
mean_lerner1 <- mean(mydata$lerner1)
price_coef1 <- coef(nliv1)["Price"]
sigma1 <- coef(nliv1)["lnsjg"]

s1 <- summary(nliv1, vcov = sandwich, diagnostics = TRUE)
diag1 <- s1$diagnostics
test_name1 <- grep("Sargan", rownames(diag1), value = TRUE)[1]
J_stat1 <- diag1[test_name1, "statistic"]
J_pval1 <- diag1[test_name1, "p-value"]

```

### QUESTION 5

*Regress the estimated marginal costs derived from the demand estimation on the "usual characteristics," following the approach in our working paper.*

The following code extract the estimated marginal costs from the model 4 (model chosen from the previous question)

**Creation of the variable short-haul and long-haul itinerary dummies and the variable Connections following the methodology of the working paper**

```{r}



library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)


segments <- mydata %>%
  dplyr::select(Firm, Origin, Dest, C1, Stops) %>%
  dplyr::distinct()


direct_dests <- segments %>%
  dplyr::filter(Stops == 0) %>%
  dplyr::select(Firm, City = Origin, Dest) %>%
  dplyr::distinct()


hub_direct_dests <- segments %>%
  dplyr::filter(Stops == 0) %>%
  dplyr::select(Firm, Hub = Origin, Dest) %>%
  dplyr::distinct()


onestop_dests <- segments %>%
  dplyr::filter(Stops == 1, !is.na(C1)) %>%
  dplyr::select(Firm, City = Origin, Hub = C1) %>%
  dplyr::distinct() %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    hub_direct_dests,
    by = c("Firm", "Hub"),
    relationship = "many-to-many"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(Firm, City, Dest) %>%
  dplyr::distinct()


total_reachable <- dplyr::bind_rows(direct_dests, onestop_dests) %>%
  dplyr::distinct() %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Firm, City) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(Total_Reachable = dplyr::n_distinct(Dest), .groups = "drop")


mydata <- mydata %>%
  dplyr::left_join(total_reachable, by = c("Firm" = "Firm", "Origin" = "City")) %>%
  dplyr::rename(Reachable_Origin = Total_Reachable) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(total_reachable, by = c("Firm" = "Firm", "Dest" = "City")) %>%
  dplyr::rename(Reachable_Dest = Total_Reachable) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(total_reachable, by = c("Firm" = "Firm", "C1" = "City")) %>%
  dplyr::rename(Reachable_Stop = Total_Reachable) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Reachable_Origin = tidyr::replace_na(Reachable_Origin, 0L),
    Reachable_Dest   = tidyr::replace_na(Reachable_Dest, 0L),
    Reachable_Stop   = tidyr::replace_na(Reachable_Stop, 0L),


    n_nodes = ifelse(Stops == 1 & !is.na(C1), 3L, 2L),


    Connections = (Reachable_Origin + Reachable_Dest +
                     ifelse(n_nodes == 3L, Reachable_Stop, 0L)) / n_nodes
  )

```

```{r}

library(tidyverse)
library(stargazer)
library(dplyr)

mydata <- mydata %>%
  mutate(mc_hat = mc4)

summary(mydata$mc_hat)
stopifnot(all(is.finite(mydata$mc_hat[!is.na(mydata$mc_hat)])))


mydata <- mydata %>%
  mutate(
    # Dummy short/long-haul
    Short = as.integer(DirectDistance <= 1500),
    Long  = as.integer(DirectDistance > 1500),

    # Intercepts (short vs long)
    Intercept_Short = Short,
    Intercept_Long  = Long,

    # Indirect
    Indirect = as.integer(Stops == 1),
    
    # Distance (short vs long)
    Distance_Short = (DirectDistance * Short), 
    Distance_Long  = (DirectDistance * Long),   

    # Interactions (short vs long)
    Indirect_Short = Indirect * Short,
    Indirect_Long  = Indirect * Long,
    
    # Connections (short vs long)
    Connections_Short = Connections * Short,
    Connections_Long  = Connections * Long)


# Formula
mc_formula <- as.formula(
  mc_hat ~ 
  Intercept_Short + Intercept_Long +
  Indirect_Short + Indirect_Long +
  Distance_Short + Distance_Long +
  Connections_Short + Connections_Long +
  DL + UA + US + WN + LCC + others - 1 )



# Estimation OLS
mc_model <- lm(mc_formula, data = mydata)

summary(mc_model)




```

### QUESTION 6

*Re-estimate the model using GMM. Compare the optimal GMM with the basic model using W = Id.*

For this question we will reuse the model established in the question 5 by using GMM estimation using the GMM optimal and the basic model using W = Id

We have reused and adapted the code given on Moodle

```{r}


library(MASS)
library(data.table)
library(tidyverse)
library(AER)
library(nloptr)
library(Matrix)


nliv <- nliv4
list_instruments <- list_instruments4
theta0d <- theta0d4
stderr_d <- stderr_d4

# Use marginal costs from the model 4 (the model chosen in the previous questions)
mydata$mc <- mydata$mc4

nobs <- nrow(mydata)

#Supply estimation

lhs <- "mc"

supply_spec <- "mc ~ Intercept_Short + Intercept_Long +
  Indirect_Short + Indirect_Long +
  Distance_Short + Distance_Long +
  Connections_Short + Connections_Long +
  DL + UA + US + WN + LCC + others - 1 "

reg_supply  <- "Intercept_Short + Intercept_Long +
  Indirect_Short + Indirect_Long +
  Distance_Short + Distance_Long +
  Connections_Short + Connections_Long +
  DL + UA + US + WN + LCC + others"

supply_est <- lm(as.formula(supply_spec), data = mydata)
summary(supply_est)

theta0s  <- supply_est$coefficients
stderr_s <- sqrt(diag(vcov(supply_est)))


theta0  <- c(theta0d, theta0s)
stderr0 <- c(stderr_d, stderr_s)


p_OLS_2SLS <- 2 * pnorm(-abs((theta0) / stderr0)) 


#Matrix for GMM
nd <- length(nliv$coefficients)
ns <- length(supply_est$coefficients)


datademand <- strsplit(list_regressors, split = " + ", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
mat_d <- as.matrix(cbind(1, mydata[, datademand]))


instrdemand <- strsplit(list_instruments, split = " + ", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
Z_d <- as.matrix(cbind(1, mydata[, instrdemand]))


Z_s <- model.matrix(as.formula(paste("~", reg_supply, "- 1")), data = mydata)


stopifnot(ncol(Z_s) == length(theta0s))


mean_moment <- function(theta){
  theta_d <- theta[1:nd]
  theta_s <- theta[(nd+1):(nd+ns)]
  

  xi  <- mydata$lnsjs0 - mat_d %*% theta_d
  xi_d <- matrix(xi, nrow = nobs, ncol = ncol(Z_d))
  mean_d <- apply(Z_d * xi_d, 2, mean)

  lambdaloc <- 1 - theta_d[3]
  alphaloc  <- -theta_d[2]
  
  markuploc <- -lambdaloc/alphaloc /
    ((1-lambdaloc)*mydata$firmshare/(1-mydata$OutsideShare) + lambdaloc*mydata$firmshare - 1)
  
  mc <- (mydata$Price - markuploc)
  
  psi <- mc - Z_s %*% theta_s
  psi_s <- matrix(psi, nrow = nrow(Z_s), ncol = ncol(Z_s))
  mean_s <- apply(Z_s * psi_s, 2, mean)
  
  as.vector(c(mean_d, mean_s))
}

varmom <- function(theta){
  theta_d <- theta[1:nd]
  theta_s <- theta[(nd+1):(nd+ns)]
  
# Demand moments
  xi  <- mydata$lnsjs0 - mat_d %*% theta_d
  xi_d <- matrix(xi, nrow = nobs, ncol = ncol(Z_d))
  momd <- Z_d * xi_d
  
# Supply moments
  lambdaloc <- 1 - theta_d[3]
  alphaloc  <- -theta_d[2]
  
  markuploc <- -lambdaloc/alphaloc /
    ((1-lambdaloc)*mydata$firmshare/(1-mydata$OutsideShare) + lambdaloc*mydata$firmshare - 1)
  
  mc <- (mydata$Price - markuploc)
  
  psi <- mc - Z_s %*% theta_s
  psi_s <- matrix(psi, nrow = nrow(Z_s), ncol = ncol(Z_s))
  moms <- Z_s * psi_s
  
  mom <- cbind(momd, moms)
  
  mombar <- apply(mom, 2, mean)
  (t(mom) %*% mom)/nobs - mombar %*% t(mombar)
}

meandmdtheta <- function(theta){
  theta_d <- theta[1:nd]
  theta_s <- theta[(nd+1):(nd+ns)]
  
  matm0 <- matrix(0, nrow = ncol(Z_d) + ncol(Z_s), ncol = nd + ns)
  

  matm0[1:ncol(Z_d), 1:nd] <- -(t(Z_d) %*% mat_d)/nobs
  

  matm0[(ncol(Z_d)+1):(ncol(Z_d)+ncol(Z_s)), (nd+1):(nd+ns)] <- -(t(Z_s) %*% Z_s)/nobs
  

  lambdaloc <- 1 - theta_d[3]
  alphaloc  <- -theta_d[2]
  
  markuploc <- -lambdaloc/alphaloc /
    ((1-lambdaloc)*mydata$firmshare/(1-mydata$OutsideShare) + lambdaloc*mydata$firmshare - 1)
  

  matm0[(ncol(Z_d)+1):(ncol(Z_d)+ncol(Z_s)), 2] <- (-1/alphaloc) * (t(Z_s) %*% markuploc)/nobs
  

  Dm <- as.vector(1/((1-lambdaloc)*mydata$firmshare/(1-mydata$OutsideShare) + lambdaloc*mydata$firmshare - 1))
  dermkupdl <- markuploc/lambdaloc + (mydata$firmshare * mydata$OutsideShare * markuploc * Dm)/(1 - mydata$OutsideShare)
  

  matm0[(ncol(Z_d)+1):(ncol(Z_d)+ncol(Z_s)), 3] <- (t(Z_s) %*% dermkupdl)/nobs
  
  matm0
}


#GMM
GMM1 <- function(theta){
  m <- mean_moment(theta)
  as.numeric(t(m) %*% m)
}

#Optimitization 
theta.init <- theta0
nparam <- length(theta.init)

lb0 <- rep(-Inf, nparam)
ub0 <- rep(+Inf, nparam)

# Bounds defined from the Moodle code
ub0[2] <- -1e-5
lb0[3] <-  1e-10
ub0[3] <-  1 - 1e-10


#Basic GMM 
Estim_NL_ID <- nloptr(
  x0 = theta.init,
  eval_f = GMM1,
  eval_grad_f = NULL,
  lb = lb0,
  ub = ub0,
  opts = list(
    "algorithm" = "NLOPT_LN_BOBYQA",
    ftol_rel = 1.e-7, ftol_abs = 1.e-9,
    xtol_rel = 1.e-7, xtol_abs = 0,
    maxeval = 100000, "print_level" = 2
  )
)

thetafin <- Estim_NL_ID$solution


W <- diag(ncol(Z_d) + ncol(Z_s))
Gm <- meandmdtheta(thetafin)
Varm <- varmom(thetafin)
Mat1 <- MASS::ginv(t(Gm) %*% W %*% Gm)


Variance_thetafin <- (Mat1 %*% t(Gm) %*% W %*% Varm %*% W %*% Gm %*% Mat1)/nobs
se_thetafin <- sqrt(diag(Variance_thetafin))
p_WI <- 2 * pnorm(-abs((thetafin) / se_thetafin)) #



#Optimal GMM two steps
W2 <- solve(Varm)

GMM2 <- function(theta){
  m <- mean_moment(theta)
  as.numeric(t(m) %*% W2 %*% m)
}

Estim_2SGMM <- nloptr(
  x0 = thetafin,
  eval_f = GMM2,
  eval_grad_f = NULL,
  lb = lb0,
  ub = ub0,
  opts = list(
    "algorithm" = "NLOPT_LN_BOBYQA",
    ftol_rel = 1.e-7, ftol_abs = 1.e-9,
    xtol_rel = 1.e-7, xtol_abs = 0,
    maxeval = 100000, "print_level" = 2
  )
)

thetafin2 <- Estim_2SGMM$solution

Gm2 <- meandmdtheta(thetafin2)
Mat2 <- MASS::ginv(t(Gm2) %*% W2 %*% Gm2)
Variance_thetafin2 <- Mat2/nobs
se_thetafin2 <- sqrt(diag(Variance_thetafin2))
p_opt <- 2 * pnorm(-abs((thetafin2) / se_thetafin2))#



#Summary Table
out <- cbind(
  theta.init,
  thetafin,
  thetafin2,
  stderr0,
  se_thetafin,
  se_thetafin2,
  p_OLS_2SLS,
  p_WI,
  p_opt
)

colnames(out) <- c("theta_init", "theta_GMM_WI", "theta_GMM_opt", "se_init(2SLS/OLS)", "se_WI", "se_opt", "p_OLS_2SLS", "p_WI", "p_opt")
print(out)

```
